title: U.S. House · Ohio's 8th District
area: Western Ohio, including Butler and Miami counties and parts of Hamilton and Clark counties (Hamilton, Fairfield, West Chester Township, Troy).

context.text: Incumbent Warren Davidson (R) advanced unopposed from the May 5, 2026 Republican primary. Vanessa Enoch (D) defeated Madaris Grant in the Democratic primary, 74.5%-25.5%. Enoch previously ran against Davidson in the 2022 and 2024 general elections, losing both.

summary.text: Davidson is the Republican incumbent in Ohio's 8th District, a seat he has held since winning a 2016 special election to succeed John Boehner. A West Point graduate and former Army infantry officer, he spent about 15 years in Ohio manufacturing before entering Congress. He chairs the National Security and Illicit Finance subcommittee of the Financial Services Committee and also serves on the Foreign Affairs Committee.

background.text: Born and raised in Sidney, Ohio; graduated from Sidney High School in 1988.
Enlisted in the Army after high school, then earned an appointment to West Point and graduated in 1995 with a degree in American history.
Served as an infantry officer in the Old Guard, the 75th Ranger Regiment and the 101st Airborne Division; left the Army in 2000.

Earned an MBA from the University of Notre Dame, then spent 15 years starting, acquiring and growing manufacturing companies in Ohio, according to his House website; Wikipedia reports he bought his father's business, West Troy Tool & Machine, in 2005 and combined it with another firm in 2014.
Served on the Concord Township, Ohio, Board of Trustees from 2004 to 2005 and chaired the Dayton Region Manufacturers Association.

Won a 15-way Republican primary and the June 7, 2016 special election to fill the remainder of former Speaker John Boehner's term; sworn in June 9, 2016, and elected to full terms since, including over Democrat Vanessa Enoch in 2018, 2020 and 2022.
Founded the Sound Money Caucus in July 2020 and chairs it; was policy chair of the House Freedom Caucus from October 2019 until July 2024.
In the 119th Congress, serves on the Financial Services Committee, where he chairs the National Security and Illicit Finance subcommittee, and on the Foreign Affairs Committee.
According to his House website, he and his wife Lisa have been married for 30 years and have two adult children.

positions.summary: His official site's pro-life page says life begins at conception and that the right to life is a freedom government has a duty to protect.
positions.quote: Life begins at conception, and the right to life is the first freedom government has a duty to protect.

record.text: Serves on the House Committee on Financial Services and the Committee on Foreign Affairs in the 119th Congress (2025-2026).

Chaired the Financial Services Subcommittee on Housing and Insurance and served as vice chairman of the Subcommittee on Digital Assets, Financial Technology and Inclusion in the 118th Congress (2023-2024).

summary.text: Vanessa Enoch is the Democratic nominee challenging incumbent Warren Davidson in Ohio's 8th District. A West Chester, Ohio, management and policy consultant who has also worked as a journalist, television reporter, college professor and dean of students, she is running for the seat for a fifth time after losing the 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024 general elections.

background.text: Born in Cincinnati, Ohio, and lives in West Chester, Ohio; graduated from Northwest High School.

Earned a bachelor's degree in criminal justice from Ohio State University (1992), an MBA from Xavier University (1999), and a doctorate in public policy from Union Institute & University (2017). In a Candidate Connection survey she describes herself as a first-generation college graduate.
Has worked as a journalist, television reporter, college professor, and dean of students.

Is president and CEO of Cultural Impact, LLC, a management and technology consulting firm; in her 2024 Candidate Connection survey she says she has run it for over 20 years and has lived and worked overseas.

Serves as board president of Vision Works, Inc. and has held board roles with the Black Greeks Speak-Social Justice Organization and Joseph Dream, a race reconciliation and healing organization; also lists membership in the American Society for Public Administrators in Cincinnati, the American Political Science Association, and the National Black MBA Association's Cincinnati chapter.
Was the Democratic nominee against Davidson in 2018, 2020, 2022 and 2024, and won the May 5, 2026 Democratic primary with 74.5% of the vote over Madaris Grant.

positions.summary: In a March 2026 campaign post on the conflict with Iran, she says the power to declare war belongs to Congress and that sustained military action requires congressional authorization.
positions.quote: The United States Constitution is clear: the power to declare war belongs to Congress.

positions.summary: In an August 2024 campaign post she says she supports reproductive rights for women and will fight for access to reproductive care.
positions.quote: I will fight every day for a woman’s right to safe, accessible, and affordable reproductive care.

positions.summary: Her campaign issues page lists raising the minimum wage among policies to make costs more affordable.
Her campaign issues page says home costs have outpaced incomes because of zoning laws and other policies, and calls for rewriting land-use rules and investing in mixed-income developments.
positions.quote: We can change course by rewriting land‑use rules, investing in mixed-income developments

researchNotes: Davidson has not completed Ballotpedia's 2026 Candidate Connection survey, and his official House website issues pages and Enoch's campaign site did not yield verbatim, current issue statements at the fetched URLs, so priorities and positions are omitted rather than inferred. Federal key votes and FEC finance totals are added separately. Enoch's biography relies on Ballotpedia; no news profile of her career was found.
